doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Playing with Don Albert and Arthur Durbin's breakdown
summary: De De recalls a Texas trip with Don Albert's big band, then Arthur Durbin losing his mind on the bandstand.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Nellie Lutcher? Yes, a year ago. She was out in the Charles. Did you ever work with Don Alba? Yeah, I went off on a month or two. Was that before Paul Barnes or after? It was almost during the time. I think we had split up and Don Alba was short with trumpet playing. I left Frank Charles and made a trip with him. Through Texas, we were joined with Don Alba. During that time, he made a trip to see his mother and father. He hadn't seen in a couple of years. So I rode back in the car with him, made my people visit, and then I went back. I played several jobs with him and went back with Paul. That's what it was done. Who was in Don Alba's band then? Oh, I don't know that much. I'm a boy. I'm a boy out of Texas. I don't see anything. Yeah, about 14 pieces. Two basses that I could remember. String and a tuba. Did you know Henry Turner? Nick Turner, they called him? Turner, Turner, Turner, Turner. I think he played tuba and trombone. I did that, I don't know. I thought maybe he was a guy in that band. I can't remember who those guys were. Lloyd Glenn was with that band at one time. He was a piano player. I think Alan Vann was another. He only had one trumpet, only had one other trumpet than himself? Himself, yeah, yeah. When you were with him? Yeah. You know Herbert Hall? Herbert Hall? Yeah, he plays baritone. Oh Hall. I didn't know Hall. I played with uh. You know, you understand that's me. One of the other. Well that's Clarence Hall. That's his brother. I know. I know. You didn't know him. You know Louis Cottrell. Oh yeah. Louis Cottrell. He used to live. Yeah. I thought maybe you'd worked with Louis Cottrell somewhere. No, no. Arthur Durbin, you ever worked with him? Yeah. Uh. I know. I know. I know. I know. I know. I know. I know. I know. Arthur Durbin. You ever worked with him? Yeah. Uh. I know. I was here in uh. The Pass. I worked with The Pass something. What was he playing then? Sax. And those he had something. Uh huh. Yeah. In fact we were playing at Jobbunny. His mind left him at the time. Arthur Durbin he lost his mind huh? Yeah. On the bandstand he started picking up all the music and said the music was his you know. He said I'm gonna set you off to the people. I'm gonna take some floor to the dance during the time. I had to send him home you know from that time on. That was all. I didn't know what to do here but I was with The Pass during that time. He was saying. Well he's alright now. Yeah he does. He went off on me. I was with The Pass during that time. He was saying. Well he's alright now. Yeah he does. He went off on me. I was with him. I see. I was working. When that happened. Did you ever know Bessie Smith Billy? Yes you did.
